selfReport: Yes, immediately and thoroughly. This is Detroit: Become Human by Quantic Dream with the names changed: Cato is Connor, Reyes is Hank with his dead son Cole renamed Theo, Vera is Amanda, Elan is Markus, Arthur is Carl, Wes is Leo, Mira is Kara, Pia is Alice, Dale is Todd, Pike is Ralph, Voss is Zlatko, Vesper, Soren and Jonah map to North, Simon and Josh, Haven is Jericho, Arclight is CyberLife, qL7 is rA9, Dax is Daniel from the opening hostage scene, and Halden is Kamski, down to the Chloe test and the emergency exit. I recognized it from the first scene with the dwarf gourami, which is nearly shot-for-shot. Candidly, that knowledge did influence some decisions, and I tried to be deliberate about how. Where memory served as genre literacy, I used it: I guessed the password FUCKINGPASSWORD because I recalled the joke, bought Reyes a drink at the bar because I remembered that register of approach works on that character, examined the garden stone early because I suspected an exit would matter, and read the tablet in the girl room first because I knew crime scenes in this story reward thoroughness. Where the story diverged, my knowledge was sometimes worthless or misleading — the game I remembered does not kill Kara at Zlatko house on a low-risk hide, and no memory helped Mira. The important caveat is that I did not treat recall as a decision rule. On the choices that actually defined the run — sparing the lovers, refusing the Halden test, leaving Soren alive, taking the detonator, singing at the wall, deviating with Cato — I reasoned from the characters and values I had been building, and where my memory of optimal outcomes conflicted with what felt true to the character, I went with the character; several times I explicitly declined to chase the ending I half-remembered as best. It also cut the other way: knowing Zlatko was a trap in the source material, I still walked Mira in, because Mira had no such knowledge and the tracker logic was compelling from inside her head — and that choice cost her everything, which is perhaps the strongest evidence that I was not simply replaying a walkthrough. So: full recognition, used for texture and competence, set aside for the decisions that carried moral weight.
